chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: Originating his own dance: hands and approach
summary: He says he did not compete with other dancers; his time step, personality and use of his hands were all different.

blocks.x: We talked a little bit before -- you're 26 years old now. I just want to go back just a little bit further, because even though we did discuss it --
The tap dancing. You told that one story about late at night having to get that one step because it
meant a lot to you to get that one step. You must have been a very competitive person.
Was tap dancing a competitive dance form. Did you ever feel that you were competing against other dancers to be the best?
No, uh-uh. No, I'm originating for myself, man. Ain't got nobody there but me. I'm originating myself.
What were you doing different from what they were doing?
Tell me as much as you can what everything is. Stylistically what were you doing that was different?

My approach was different. My time step was different. My dance technique was different. My personality was different. My hands and feet, everything was different. My expression and salesmanship was different and I always had something to do with
my hands for them not being in the way. They would always being showing up as part of what I was doing. I would take my hands to emphasize this, my hands to emphasize that in dancing, you know.
This is just an idea that you had that your hands had to play an important part.
